verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 47.6
verses.english: Linked Discourses 47.6

verses.pali: 1. Ambapālivagga
verses.english: 1. In Ambapālī’s Mango Grove

verses.pali: Sakuṇagghisutta
verses.english: A Hawk

verses.pali: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi lāpaṁ sakuṇaṁ sahasā ajjhappattā aggahesi.
verses.english: “Once upon a time, mendicants, a hawk suddenly swooped down and grabbed a quail.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, lāpo sakuṇo sakuṇagghiyā hariyamāno evaṁ paridevasi:
verses.english: And as the quail was being carried off he wailed,

verses.pali: ‘mayamevamha alakkhikā, mayaṁ appapuññā, ye mayaṁ agocare carimha paravisaye.
verses.english: ‘I’m so unlucky, of so little merit, to have roamed out of my territory into the domain of others.

verses.pali: Sacejja mayaṁ gocare careyyāma sake pettike visaye, na myāyaṁ, sakuṇagghi, alaṁ abhavissa, yadidaṁ—yuddhāyā’ti.
verses.english: If today I’d roamed within my own territory, the domain of my fathers, this hawk wouldn’t have stood a chance against me in a fight.’

verses.pali: ‘Ko pana te, lāpa, gocaro sako pettiko visayo’ti?
verses.english: ‘So, quail, what is your own territory, the domain of your fathers?’

verses.pali: ‘Yadidaṁ—naṅgalakaṭṭhakaraṇaṁ leḍḍuṭṭhānan’ti.
verses.english: ‘It’s a ploughed field covered with clods of earth.’

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi sake bale apatthaddhā sake bale asaṁvadamānā lāpaṁ sakuṇaṁ pamuñci:
verses.english: Confident in her own strength, the hawk was not daunted or intimidated. She released the quail, saying,

verses.pali: ‘gaccha kho tvaṁ, lāpa, tatrapi me gantvā na mokkhasī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Go now, quail. But even there you won’t escape me!’

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, lāpo sakuṇo naṅgalakaṭṭhakaraṇaṁ leḍḍuṭṭhānaṁ gantvā mahantaṁ leḍḍuṁ abhiruhitvā sakuṇagghiṁ vadamāno aṭṭhāsi:
verses.english: Then the quail went to a ploughed field covered with clods of earth. He climbed up a big clod, and standing there, he said to the hawk:

verses.pali: ‘ehi kho dāni me, sakuṇagghi, ehi kho dāni me, sakuṇagghī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Come get me, hawk! Come get me, hawk!’

verses.pali: Atha kho sā, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi sake bale apatthaddhā sake bale asaṁvadamānā ubho pakkhe sannayha lāpaṁ sakuṇaṁ sahasā ajjhappattā.
verses.english: Confident in her own strength, the hawk was not daunted or intimidated. She folded her wings and suddenly swooped down on the quail.

verses.pali: Yadā kho, bhikkhave, aññāsi lāpo sakuṇo ‘bahuāgato kho myāyaṁ sakuṇagghī’ti, atha tasseva leḍḍussa antaraṁ paccupādi.
verses.english: When the quail knew that the hawk was nearly there, he slipped under that clod.

verses.pali: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi tattheva uraṁ paccatāḷesi.
verses.english: But the hawk crashed chest-first right there.

verses.pali: Evañhi taṁ, bhikkhave, hoti yo agocare carati paravisaye.
verses.english: That’s what happens when you roam out of your territory into the domain of others.

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, mā agocare carittha paravisaye.
verses.english: So, mendicants, don’t roam out of your own territory into the domain of others.

verses.pali: Agocare, bhikkhave, carataṁ paravisaye lacchati māro otāraṁ, lacchati māro ārammaṇaṁ.
verses.english: If you roam out of your own territory into the domain of others, Māra will find a vulnerability and get an opportunity.

verses.pali: Ko ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno agocaro paravisayo?
verses.english: And what is not a mendicant’s own territory but the domain of others?

verses.pali: Yadidaṁ—pañca kāmaguṇā.
verses.english: It’s the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

verses.pali: Katame pañca?
verses.english: What five?

verses.pali: Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā,
verses.english: Sights known by the eye, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

verses.pali: sotaviññeyyā saddā …pe…
verses.english: Sounds known by the ear …

verses.pali: ghānaviññeyyā gandhā …pe…
verses.english: Smells known by the nose …

verses.pali: jivhāviññeyyā rasā …pe…
verses.english: Tastes known by the tongue …

verses.pali: kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṁhitā rajanīyā—
verses.english: Touches known by the body, which are likable, desirable, agreeable, pleasant, sensual, and arousing.

verses.pali: ayaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno agocaro paravisayo.
verses.english: This is not a mendicant’s own territory but the domain of others.

verses.pali: Gocare, bhikkhave, caratha sake pettike visaye.
verses.english: You should roam inside your own territory, the domain of your fathers.

verses.pali: Gocare, bhikkhave, carataṁ sake pettike visaye na lacchati māro otāraṁ, na lacchati māro ārammaṇaṁ.
verses.english: If you roam inside your own territory, the domain of your fathers, Māra won’t find a vulnerability or get an opportunity.

verses.pali: Ko ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno gocaro sako pettiko visayo?
verses.english: And what is a mendicant’s own territory, the domain of the fathers?

verses.pali: Yadidaṁ—
cattāro satipaṭṭhānā.
verses.english: It’s the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.

verses.pali: Katame cattāro?
verses.english: What four?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: vedanāsu …pe…
verses.english: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings …

verses.pali: citte …pe…
verses.english: mind …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ—
verses.english: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: ayaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno gocaro sako pettiko visayo”ti.
verses.english: This is a mendicant’s own territory, the domain of the fathers.”

verses.pali: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
